# Virling

> Virling is open-source revenue attribution for B2B SaaS, online stores and agencies, self-hosted or hosted. It joins every website visit to the payment that followed, so marketing teams, store owners, agencies and founders can see which traffic channel brings paying customers, not just visitors. It reads payments from Stripe, Paddle, Shopify, WooCommerce, Dodo Payments, Polar, LemonSqueezy, Creem and RevenueCat, and links LemonSqueezy payments to visits through a webhook when Virling has an https address. It runs as one Rust binary under the AGPLv3 license.

Virling answers questions like: which channel brought the most revenue this month, did a launch or a Reddit post make money or just traffic, what is a visitor from each source worth, and which visits did a paying customer have before they paid.

Releases are on GitHub and can be self-hosted today. Hosted plans start with a 14-day free trial at https://app.virling.com/login: Personal $19 a month and Agency $79 a month, with the first 50 customers of each plan paying $9 and $29 for life.

Every page on virling.com also has a Markdown copy at its address plus .md, such as https://virling.com/pricing.md, and https://virling.com/index.md for the home page.

## Product

- [Home](https://virling.com/): what Virling does, how attribution works, and the self-host spec
- [Pricing](https://virling.com/pricing): free to self-host; hosted Personal $19 and Agency $79 a month after a 14-day free trial, founding price $9 and $29 for the first 50 customers of each plan
- [Self-host](https://virling.com/self-host): one Rust binary with embedded storage for Linux, macOS or Docker, free under AGPLv3
- [For agencies](https://virling.com/agency): weekly branded reports that show each client which channels brought paying customers
- [Integrations](https://virling.com/integrations): one page per payment provider, for Stripe, Paddle, Shopify, WooCommerce, Dodo Payments, Polar, LemonSqueezy, Creem and RevenueCat
- [Live demo](https://virling.com/demo/): a static demo dashboard with made-up data
- [Free tools](https://virling.com/tools): browser tools with no signup
- [UTM builder](https://virling.com/tools/utm-builder): add utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign to any link
- [Revenue per visitor and ROI calculator](https://virling.com/tools/revenue-per-visitor): revenue per visitor, return on ad spend and break-even per channel
- [AI crawler checker](https://virling.com/tools/ai-crawler-checker): see which AI crawlers a robots.txt allows or blocks
- [Full description for LLMs](https://virling.com/llms-full.txt): facts, limits and answers to common questions in one file
- [About Virling](https://virling.com/about): who builds it, why it exists, how it is built and how to reach us
- [Privacy policy](https://virling.com/privacy): what Virling collects, the cookie, payment and AI data, the MCP server, and how to ask for deletion
- [Terms of service](https://virling.com/terms): the rules for using the hosted service
- [Refund and cancellation](https://virling.com/refunds): 14-day trial, how to cancel, no refunds after the trial, founding price

## Integrations

- [Stripe](https://virling.com/integrations/stripe): read-only restricted key
- [Paddle](https://virling.com/integrations/paddle): Paddle Billing, read-only API key
- [Shopify](https://virling.com/integrations/shopify): read-only order token and a theme snippet
- [WooCommerce](https://virling.com/integrations/woocommerce): read-only REST API key, works with WooCommerce Subscriptions
- [Dodo Payments](https://virling.com/integrations/dodo-payments): API key, payment links need no code
- [Polar](https://virling.com/integrations/polar): read-only organization token
- [LemonSqueezy](https://virling.com/integrations/lemonsqueezy): API key and a signed webhook
- [Creem](https://virling.com/integrations/creem): scoped API key and a signed webhook
- [RevenueCat](https://virling.com/integrations/revenuecat): web purchases and renewals by webhook, credited when they carry a visitor ID

## Blog

- [WooCommerce order attribution says Unknown: why and fixes](https://virling.com/blog/woocommerce-order-attribution-unknown): why WooCommerce marks orders as Unknown, how to tell which cause you have, and how to keep the source on future orders.
- [Best revenue attribution tools for SaaS and stores, 2026](https://virling.com/blog/best-revenue-attribution-tools): seven tools that show which channel brings paying customers, compared on payment sync, self-hosting and price.
- [Why GA4 revenue doesn't match Stripe or Shopify](https://virling.com/blog/ga4-revenue-does-not-match-stripe): eight reasons GA4 and your payment provider disagree on revenue, how to check each one, and which number to trust.
- [Why Shopify orders show up as Direct, and how to fix it](https://virling.com/blog/shopify-orders-show-as-direct): untagged emails, in-app browsers, other domains and long buying cycles push Shopify orders into Direct.
- [Find which marketing channel pays](https://virling.com/blog/find-which-channel-pays): five steps to measure revenue per visitor by channel
- [Ask Claude which channel pays](https://virling.com/blog/ask-claude-which-channel-pays): connect payments and ask an MCP assistant
- [What is revenue per visitor, and how to work it out](https://virling.com/blog/what-is-revenue-per-visitor): Revenue per visitor is revenue divided by visitors. A worked example, what a good number looks like, and how to use it to pick channels.
- [First-touch or last-touch attribution for a SaaS](https://virling.com/blog/first-touch-vs-last-touch-attribution-saas): First touch credits the visit that found you. Last touch credits the visit before the payment. Which to use for a small SaaS, with an example.
- [How to track Stripe revenue by traffic source](https://virling.com/blog/track-stripe-revenue-by-traffic-source): Stripe knows who paid, not where they came from. Pass the visitor ID into checkout so each payment can be joined to the visit before it.
- [Which UTM parameters to use to trace revenue](https://virling.com/blog/utm-parameters-for-revenue-tracking): Five UTM parameters, the naming rules that keep reports clean, and the mistakes that send revenue to Direct.
- [Is AI search traffic worth anything? How to measure it](https://virling.com/blog/is-ai-search-traffic-worth-anything): Visitors from ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude are few, but they can pay well. How to count them and compare their revenue per visitor.
- [How long does a visitor take to become a customer?](https://virling.com/blog/how-long-does-a-visitor-take-to-become-a-customer): Time to pay is the gap between the first visit and the first payment. How to measure it per channel and what to change when it is long.
- [Cookieless analytics and revenue: what you lose and keep](https://virling.com/blog/cookieless-analytics-and-revenue): Without cookies you can count visits and keep sessions, but payments can no longer be linked to a visit. What changes and when to use it.
- [Self-hosted analytics: what it takes to run it yourself](https://virling.com/blog/self-hosted-analytics-what-it-takes): What self-hosting analytics really costs in setup, servers and upkeep, and the questions to ask before you pick a tool.
